title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 111-112): Grothendieck is listing Lefschetz-type statements, 'modulo finite groups' and 'except p', for groups of algebraic cycles on a smooth projective X of dimension n with a smooth hyperplane section Y and Lefschetz operator L (the page also writes E for L). The notation appears to be: 𝒜_r = cycles modulo rational equivalence (Chow groups); 𝒜_a = cycles modulo algebraic equivalence; superscript a (or τ) = the subgroup of classes algebraically equivalent to zero, which plays the role of the odd cohomology H^{2i-1}. 𝒜_π seems to denote the same 'abelian variety' part, whether rational equivalence again or its image in the intermediate abelian variety. Upper indices are codimension, lower indices dimension.

The previous page conjectures two things:
- hard Lefschetz L^{n-2i}: 𝒜^i_a(X) → 𝒜^{n-i}_a(X) is bijective mod finite groups;
- L^{n-2i+1}: 𝒜^i_r(X)^a → 𝒜^{n-i+1}_r(X)^a is bijective mod finite groups;
plus a weak-Lefschetz surjectivity for push-forward from Y.

This page draws consequences for two quasi-affine varieties.

(2') Let U = X - Y, a smooth affine variety. By the localization sequence CH_i(Y) → CH_i(X) → CH_i(U) → 0, one has 𝒜_r(U) = 𝒜_r(X)/Im 𝒜_r(Y), and similarly for algebraic equivalence. Weak Lefschetz in homology (H_k(Y) → H_k(X) onto for k ≤ n-1) then predicts:
- 𝒜^r_i(U) = 0 for 2i ≤ n-2. The algebraically trivial part is governed by H_{2i+1}, so one needs 2i+1 ≤ n-1.
- 𝒜^a_i(U) = 0 for 2i = n-1. Only H_{2i} = H_{n-1} matters here.
Both are qualified 'except p?'. This is a Chow-theoretic analogue of Artin vanishing: low-dimensional cycle groups of a smooth affine variety should be trivial mod finite groups.

(3') Let E be the punctured affine cone over X ⊂ P^N. It is quasi-affine and smooth of dimension n+1, and a G_m-bundle over X. The localization sequence gives CH^i(E) = coker(L: CH^{i-1}(X) → CH^i(X)). Hard Lefschetz mod finite groups gives:
- coker L on 𝒜_a is finite for 2i ≥ n+1;
- coker L on the algebraically trivial part is finite for 2i ≥ n+2.
In the complementary ranges coker L should be the primitive part. The N.B. formulates this as: 𝒜^i_a(E) ≅ M^i_a(X), the primitive part of the 'algebraic cohomology', for 2i ≤ n; and 𝒜^i_π(E)^a ≅ I^i(X), the primitive part of the intermediate abelian variety, for 2i ≤ n+1.

So Chow groups of the punctured cone compute the primitive Lefschetz pieces of X's cycle groups. These are Chow and Griffiths-group analogues of the classical computation of the cohomology of the link of a cone singularity.
errors: Definitions of the primitive parts are off by one. The primitive part in codimension i (the cokernel of L from degree i-1) is Ker(L^{n-2i+1}: 𝒜^i_a → 𝒜^{n-i+1}_a), not Ker L^{n-2i}. By the hard Lefschetz statement on the previous page, L^{n-2i} is bijective mod finite groups, so Grothendieck's M^i_a would be finite. Likewise I^i should be Ker(L^{n-2i+2}: 𝒜^i(X)^a → 𝒜^{n-i+2}(X)^a), since L^{n-2i+1} is the conjectured isomorphism. The ranges of validity (2i ≤ n, resp. 2i ≤ n+1) are correct.
'dim 2n+1' for the punctured cone should be n+1 (assuming the reading is right).

If 𝒜_r means rational equivalence over C (or any big algebraically closed field), the vanishing statements are false in general. For n=2, i=0, CH_0(U) = CH_0(X)/Im CH_0(Y) is huge for surfaces with p_g > 0 (Mumford 1969, Bloch-Srinivas). The underlying push-forward surjectivity likewise fails.

Likewise 𝒜^a_1(U) = 0 for affine threefolds (2i = n-1, n=3) contradicts Clemens' infinitely generated Griffiths group: for a general quintic threefold, Griff(X)⊗Q has infinite rank, while the image of curves on a surface Y has finitely generated NS.

The statements are consistent only over small base fields: over Q̄ via Bloch-Beilinson, or over finite fields / F̄_p via Bass-Tate-Beilinson type conjectures. There 'except p' would naturally mean 'except p-primary torsion'. The page does not specify the base field.

ideas.what: Localization: CH(U) = CH(X)/Im CH(Y) for U = X - Y
ideas.modern_name: localization exact sequence for Chow groups

ideas.what: Lefschetz-type conjectures for cycles modulo rational and algebraic equivalence mod finite groups, applied to give vanishing of low-dimensional Chow groups / Griffiths groups of smooth affine varieties
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz conjectures for Chow groups / Hartshorne's questions on cycles of small codimension; Chow-theoretic Artin vanishing (cf. Bloch-Beilinson consequences, Paranjape connectivity)
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures (1968) treat only cycles modulo homological equivalence

ideas.what: Chow groups of the punctured affine cone equal coker of L, hence the primitive part of the cycle groups of X (algebraic part and intermediate-abelian-variety part)
ideas.modern_name: Chow groups of cones / G_m-bundles; primitive decomposition of Chow groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Srinivas and others on Chow groups of cone singularities (1980s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly links hard and weak Lefschetz for cycle groups mod finite groups (and 'except p') to vanishing of Chow groups of affine varieties and to the cycle groups of punctured cones as primitive parts. This anticipates questions later posed by Hartshorne (1975) and the Bloch-Beilinson picture. It is a cycle-level analogue of Artin vanishing and of the cohomology of links.
missed.quote: 2i ≤ n-2 ... 𝒜^r_i(U) = 0 (exc. p ?) ... 𝒜^i_a(E) ≃ M^i_a(X) mod gr. finis si 2i ≤ n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck considered Lefschetz for Chow groups (not just homological cycles) around 1965-71. The formulation is refuted over C (Mumford, Clemens) but meaningful over Q̄ and finite fields. This is a historical precursor rather than a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: An unpublished early formulation of Lefschetz conjectures at the level of Chow groups and Griffiths groups, with clean affine and cone consequences. Historically interesting, but the ideas reappear (and are partly refuted over C) in later literature, and the page contains index slips.
transcription_corrections: '(variété quasi-affine non sing. de dim 2n+1)' – mathematically should be n+1; the handwriting may read 'n+1'.
The operator written E on the previous page is the Lefschetz operator L, as on this page.
In (2') the lower index on 𝒜^r_i(U), 𝒜^a_i(U) is a dimension index, whereas upper i elsewhere is codimension.
The crossed-out line reads '𝒜^i_π(E)^a ≃ B^i_π(X) mod groupes finis si 2i ≤ n+1' and was replaced by the I^i(X) system.
